title: Span-aware length bucket orchestrator to reduce padding and improve kernel fit
author: Evan Morales
description: Motivation: real production traffic often contains mixed-length requests where naive length bucketing either over-pads short requests or produces small batches for long requests that don't align well with optimized GPU kernels and KV-cache prefill windows. This PR introduces a span-aware length bucket orchestrator: a hybrid bucketing algorithm that groups incoming sequences into contiguous length spans (span = [Lmin, Lmax]) chosen to minimize expected padding cost while preserving opportunities to select kernel variants and prefill KV cache windows efficiently. The orchestrator considers three signals: sequence-length distribution, kernel fit profiles (preferred block sizes per model), and KV prefetch locality (recent sequence prefixes that share KV cache state). It produces dynamic span buckets that are stable over tens of milliseconds to allow continuous batching to form, but adapt quickly to distribution shifts. Key changes: - New scheduler module runtime/batcher/span_orchestrator.py that computes span buckets using a lightweight quantile sweep and a kernel-fit cost table taken from compilation profiles. - Integration hook into the continuous batcher allowing buckets to be pinned for a short TTL to improve kernel-run coalescing and KV cache reuse. - KV prefetch hint propagation: handlers now attach a span_id and prefill_hint to requests so the KV cache prefetcher can align window boundaries across the bucket. - New config knobs: span_ttl_ms (defaults to 50ms), max_span_width_pct (caps bucket width relative to median length), and kernel_fit_weight (tradeoff between padding cost and kernel alignment). - Metrics and dashboards: added span.bucket_count, span.avg_padding_tokens, span.kv_prefill_hit_rate, plus detailed per-model kernel_fit_ratio. Implementation notes: the orchestrator balances a simple cost model (pad_cost + kernel_misalignment_penalty * kernel_fit_weight - kv_hit_benefit) performed in O(k log k) per quantile sweep where k is small (default 20 quantiles). We intentionally avoid an NP-hard combinatorial optimizer to keep overhead < 200us per decision on a serving thread. Benchmarks & results: ran against the benchmark-lab mixed-seqlen profile and live Canary traffic in us-east-1 (internal canary). Observed results (canary -> full rollout): - pad tokens reduced by 11.2% (median across models), with best-case 18% on bimodal workloads - end-to-end throughput (tokens/s) improved 5.8% on average, up to 9.4% on medium-length-dominated workloads - p50 token latency unchanged; p95 token latency +1.8ms median (within SLA for most customers) - KV cache prefill hit rate improved by 6.1% for models with large KV windows (improved amortized KV cost) - CPU overhead for orchestration decision ~120us on a 2.5GHz core (measured under load), acceptable for our runtime thread budget Stability & safety: - Feature-gated behind span_length_orchestrator_enabled (opt-in for Dedicated and Private; enabled behind rollout flag for Hosted) - Canary plan: 10% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback thresholds on p99 latency and error-rate deltas - Fallback: if kernel_fit_ratio drops more than 15% in any minute, orchestrator enters safe-mode and falls back to fixed quantile bucketing while keeping KV hints off Migration and ops: - Added a migration doc in docs/ops/span_orchestrator.md describing config knobs, recommended values for small/medium/large models, and a recommended canary checklist. - Exposed metrics to Redwood Console and added sample alerts: alert/span_padding_regression and alert/span_kernel_regression Tests: - Unit tests for the cost model and quantile sweep - Integration tests in perf-canary harness simulating workload shifts and KV cache warm/cold transitions - End-to-end perf jobs in benchmark-lab with historical traces to validate non-regression on representative workloads Related work and context: builds on earlier bucketed-batching and kernel-fit efforts but differs by explicitly trading off padding vs kernel alignment and by adding KV prefill hinting. See ENG-4821 for product acceptance criteria. Rollout & monitoring: released behind the flag on 2026-02-20 to internal customers and ran canary through 2026-02-27. Merged after successful canary with metrics meeting acceptance windows. This PR is intentionally conservative: cost model weights are tunable without code changes, and operators can disable the feature immediately via the flag.

release_notes: Introduces a span-aware length bucket orchestrator that reduces padding tokens and improves throughput by dynamically creating contiguous length spans optimized for padding cost, kernel fit, and KV prefill locality. Feature is behind a flag and rolled out via canary. Metrics: ~11% pad reduction median and ~6% KV hit improvement in canary.
